summary: Resolved review-v1 ISSUE-1 (MEDIUM, APPLY). naverCoordToken used a broad [-180,180] guard applied to BOTH lat and lng, so an impossible latitude (e.g. 120) still produced a Naver directions URL instead of failing soft. Fix (web/src/naver-map-links.ts): directionsSegment now validates axis-specific WGS84 bounds before tokenizing — latitude must be finite and within [-90,90], longitude finite and within [-180,180] (new isValidLat/isValidLng guards) — and returns null otherwise, so naverTransitDirectionsUrl returns null for any invalid latitude/longitude pair and the transition row renders no directions link (fail soft). The token formula stays isolated; naverCoordToken keeps its broad [-180,180] formula-overflow guard (it is a single-coordinate encoder and cannot know which axis it is). +1 helper test: lat 120 → null, lat -120 → null (out of latitude range despite being inside the broad token range), and valid boundary coordinates (lat 90/-90, lng 180/-180) still produce a non-null URL; existing invalid-longitude and NaN/Infinity cases remain covered. Frontend-only; change limited to the one helper file (+ its test). No Today render change, no shared/server/DB/migration/gateway/config change; the Naver-search path, valid-coordinate directions path, and all travel/feasibility/transition behavior are unchanged. RESOLVED appended below the sentinel. Committed 7662b7a.
